message.content:
I'm building a reusable job-search skill. Earlier research covered EU-focused boards (euremotejobs.com, remoterocketship.com, himalayas.app, arbeitnow API, remoteok API, aijobs.net) and ATS search via WebSearch `allowed_domains` (jobs.ashbyhq.com, job-boards.greenhouse.io, job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io, jobs.smartrecruiters.com, join.com, jobs.personio.com, jobs.lever.co). Those are settled — don't re-test them.

New requirement: the candidate is based in Venice, Italy and is ALSO open to (a) roles outside the EU, and (b) **contractor / freelance / B2B / project-based** engagements, not just salaried employment. He's an AI/automation engineer (n8n, LLM agents, RAG, API integrations, TypeScript, Laravel, low-code) with ~3 years experience and product-ownership background.

Use ONLY WebSearch and WebFetch. Do NOT use curl, wget, python requests, or any bash-based fetching — prohibited here. If a domain is blocked, note it once and move on; never retry more than once.

Test, in this priority order:

1. **Contract/freelance marketplaces and boards** — which are WebFetch-readable and give real listings with title/rate/scope/link?
   - braintrust.com (app.usebraintrust.com/jobs), contra.com, gun.io, toptal.com, upwork.com, contractjobs / worksome.com, malt.fr (big in EU freelancing), freelancermap.com, useparallel/Lemon.io, remotive.com, workingnomads.com, nodesk.co
   Also test whether adding contract-intent keywords to WebSearch with `allowed_domains` on the ATS domains surfaces contract roles: e.g. query `AI automation engineer contract remote` restricted to jobs.ashbyhq.com and job-boards.greenhouse.io, and a query using words like "contractor", "freelance", "fixed-term", "B2B", "6-month contract".

2. **Global / US-company remote boards where an Italy-based person is eligible** — do any expose a filter for "hire anywhere" / "worldwide" / "Europe eligible"? Test:
   - remotive.com, workingnomads.com, nodesk.co, wellfound.com remote filter, otta.com, jobgether.com (it kept appearing as an aggregator — is it actually fetchable and useful?), dailyremote / justremote, weworkremotely alternatives
   For each, report whether the listing states region eligibility (critical — the biggest time-waster is a "remote" role that is secretly US-only).

3. **AI-company-specific hiring pages worth checking directly** — run 2-3 WebSearch queries to identify which well-known AI/agent/automation companies currently list Europe-remote or worldwide-remote engineering roles (e.g. n8n, Zapier, Make, Tray.ai, ElevenLabs, Mistral, Hugging Face, LangChain, Vercel, Supabase, Cursor/Anysphere, Deel, Remote.com). Report the verbatim careers-page or ATS URL for any you confirm are fetchable, and note which of them explicitly hire contractors or "anywhere in the world".

Return a concise factual report:
- Table: source → fetchable? → gives contract roles? → states region eligibility? → verbatim working URL template
- Which contract-intent search keywords actually surfaced contract roles on ATS domains (with the verbatim query)
- Blocked/useless sources with the specific failure mode
- Your top 5 recommendations for (i) contract work and (ii) global-remote-eligible-from-Italy work
- Any trap you noticed (e.g. "remote" listings that are secretly region-locked, agencies masquerading as end employers)

Every claim must be backed by a call you actually made. Aim for ~28 tool calls max.

content.content:
# Project Listings Analysis

## Visible Project Information

The page displays **1,013 jobs & projects** with the following details per listing:

**Data Points Shown:**
- ✓ Project title
- ✓ Location/remote status
- ✓ Contract duration (where specified)
- ✗ Rate/hourly pay (generally absent)
- ✓ Region/country information

## Sample Listings Structure

Each posting includes:
- **Title**: e.g., "Office 365 Specialist Needed full time in Johannesburg South Africa"
- **Location**: City and country (e.g., "Johannesburg, South Africa")
- **Workplace type**: On-site, Hybrid, or Remote
- **Contract type**: Freelance or Agency contract
- **Duration**: Range like "12 months+", "6 months+", or "3 months+"
- **Start date**: "ASAP" or specific month/year

## Notable Gaps

Most listings **do not display rates or hourly/daily fees** on this view. A few UK-based agency contract roles mention daily rates in their titles (e.g., "£600 per day"), but this is inconsistent and embedded in the title rather than a dedicated rate field.

The page emphasizes "0% commission, free to apply, direct client contact" rather than pricing transparency at the listing level.
